neighbours.label: the last word of a scholarly title in a reference list, where the title ends (before '. Journal', '. Ph.D.', 'by')
fire: Smith J, Lee K (2015). Dopamine release in the rat striatum. Journal of Neurochemistry 133: 45-52.
Garcia M. Soil erosion on terraced hillsides of northern Peru. PhD thesis, University of Leeds, 2009.
Chen L, et al. Regulation of root growth by auxin transport. Plant Cell 21, 1500-1512 (2010).
Brown T. A short history of the Hanseatic League. Cambridge University Press, 1998.
Okafor N, Hall R. Bird migration timing across the Sahel. Ecology Letters, 2018; 21(4): 600-611.
Weber H (2003). Coastal flooding risk in the Netherlands. Natural Hazards 30: 211-230.
Kim S, Park J. Machine learning methods for protein structure prediction. Bioinformatics 36, 2020.
Rossi A. Trade networks in medieval Venice. Journal of Economic History 54 (1994): 12-34.
quiet: Dopamine release in the rat striatum rises sharply after a reward is given.
Soil erosion on terraced hillsides of northern Peru has worsened since the rains.
Root growth is regulated by auxin, which moves from cell to cell in the plant.
The Hanseatic League controlled much of the trade along northern coasts.
Bird migration across the Sahel now starts a few days earlier each decade.
Coastal flooding in the Netherlands is held back by dikes and pumps.
Machine learning has changed how researchers predict protein structures.
Merchants in medieval Venice built trade networks that reached far east.

notes: Top examples: '...Primary Visual Cortex (V1). Journal', '...embryonic development. Nature Genetics', '...Simulations. J. Comput. Chem.'. The + pole fires at the head of a title before its subtitle colon (and promotes ':'), so the pair reads title-continues-with-subtitle vs title-ends. Near misses: same topics in plain prose, no citation.
